The Save America's Rural Hospitals Act (H.R.3684) proves Washington's priorities are upside down. While Section 101 throws temporary lifelines to rural hospitals by tweaking Medicare sequestration, the real crisis stems from decades of bureaucratic mismanagement and Medicaid bloat. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act's proposed $800B Medicaid cuts would gut rural healthcare - Manatt Health's analysis shows rural facilities losing 21% of Medicaid funding, totaling $70B over a decade. This isn't fiscal responsibility; it's robbing Peter to pay Paul while preserving D.C.'s pet projects.

The solution isn't more Band-Aid bills but structural reform: slash redundant administrative layers in healthcare bureaucracy, end Medicaid fraud (estimated at $100B annually), and redirect funds to frontline care. Rural hospitals don't need complex reimbursement formulas - they need Washington to stop burning cash on consultants and middlemen while communities lose emergency rooms.
